overview.description: Aseptic technique is easy to learn, impossible to master. Technical errors only matter if they introduce non-experimental variables. If you reliably grow contamination-free plates and verify results, the nuances of your set-up don't matter - results are what count.
objectives: perform sterile transfers near a flame
use an inoculating loop/wand and a glass spreader
understand why controls catch non-experimental variables

instructions.title: Flame your tools
instructions.description: Flame the inoculating loop to red-hot, let it cool a moment, then pick a colony or dip into culture - always within the cone of protection.

instructions.title: Streak for single colonies
instructions.description: Streak in quadrants, flaming the loop between sectors, to isolate single colonies.

instructions.title: Spread evenly
instructions.description: Use a sterile glass spreader to distribute liquid culture across a plate for even lawn or countable colonies.

instructions.title: Always run controls
instructions.description: Include positive and negative controls so that contamination or reagent failure is immediately diagnosable.

submission.description: Streak a plate to obtain isolated single colonies and photograph the result. Include a contamination-free negative control plate.
